 We are seeking an innovative Research Fellow in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) to play a key role in an ambitious new research project exploring the future of generative AI in the creative industries.

 The opportunity 

 MIMETIC is a three-year programme funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC), developing the UK's first audiovisual foundation model for the creative industries. A foundation model is a large-scale AI model that can be adapted to support a wide range of applications, tools and products. Currently, most generative AI models are developed outside the UK using scraped, copyrighted material, making them legally contested and unsuitable for many UK studios.

 MIMETIC addresses these challenges by using sound, music, image and video data sourced, generated and controlled by the project. Developed and retained in British hands, the model will enable rights holders to customise it using their own data and hardware. Deliverables include open-source libraries, generation and editing software, and trustworthy foundation models, developed and evaluated with professional companies across animation, games, visual effects and broadcast.

 As the project's HCI researcher, you will explore how creative practitioners use audiovisual foundation models and ensure their needs shape the models and tools being developed. Working directly with professionals across animation, games, visual effects, broadcast and music, you will study existing workflows, design and conduct research studies and workshops, co-design and prototype interfaces and interaction techniques, and evaluate the project's models and tools in practice. 

 The role requires a strong grounding in HCI research methods and sufficient technical knowledge of machine learning to develop working prototypes and collaborate effectively with machine learning engineers. 

 This is a 0.5 FTE post, supervised by Professor Rebecca Fiebrink. You will work alongside two Research Fellows managed by Professor Mick Grierson and the wider MIMETIC research team and industry partners.

 About you 

 You will hold a PhD (or equivalent experience) in Human-Computer Interaction, Creative Computing, Computer Science, Design or a related area, with a focus on creative practice and tools. Candidates in the final year of a PhD, or without a PhD but with peer-reviewed publications at ACM or comparable international conferences (such as CHI or NIME), will also be considered. 

 You will have demonstrable experience of designing and conducting HCI research with professional or expert users, including qualitative and quantitative studies, workshops, co-design and evaluation, alongside an understanding of ethical research with human participants.

 You will have experience designing and building interactive prototypes incorporating machine learning models, with programming skills (for example, Python and JavaScript) to work with generative models and machine learning engineers. 

 You will also have knowledge of creative media and/or music production, including the tools and workflows used in animation, games, visual effects, broadcast or music, and a record of research dissemination through publications or comparable activity. 

 You will be able to plan and prioritise your own work and that of others, monitor progress, resolve problems and identify practical solutions to ensure objectives are achieved. You will also contribute to advancing professional practice, research or scholarly activity in your specialist area.

 To apply please click the apply button. 

 Closing date: 6 December 2026 at 23:55.

 About the role 

 We are seeking an ambitious Lead Clinical Research Scientist to join an exciting Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between the University of Leicester and Carelight Limited, trading as Carelight Weartech. Based primarily at Carelight’s premises in Loughborough, you will lead the scientific and technical delivery of a pioneering project developing and validating an AI-enabled wearable health-monitoring device based on patented Opto-Physiological Monitoring (OPM) technology. Working at the intersection of physiological measurement, signal processing, machine learning and clinical data interpretation, you will analyse complex physiological datasets, contribute to the development and refinement of AI-driven approaches to biomarker extraction, support clinical validation and help integrate OPM technology into a next-generation wearable device. 

 This is an opportunity to take ownership of an innovative project with potential clinical, commercial and societal impact, supporting the ambition to improve remote patient monitoring and earlier identification of deterioration in stroke and cardiovascular patients. You will act as a key link between Carelight and the University of Leicester, helping to embed new scientific and analytical capability within the company while benefiting from structured KTP development opportunities and an annual £2,000 personal training and development budget. The University’s Department of Cardiovascular Sciences has an international reputation for cardiovascular research and strong links with the NHS, providing a highly collaborative environment in which clinical and scientific research can translate into benefits for patients. 

 About you 

 You will have a Master’s degree in Life Sciences or a relevant related discipline, such as Clinical Research, Health Sciences or Biomedical Sciences, alongside experience of handling physiological measurement datasets and collecting, evaluating and interpreting clinical research data. You will bring strong analytical problem-solving skills, relevant analytical expertise and an understanding of clinical pathways and where emerging technology could be applied, tested and deployed. Experience of signal processing, machine learning, AI-enabled biomarker extraction, wearable technologies, medical devices or digital health would be advantageous, as would a PhD or equivalent relevant industrial experience. 

 Curious, proactive and impact-driven, you will have the organisational skills and leadership potential to take responsibility for a complex project while working effectively both independently and with multidisciplinary academic, clinical and industry colleagues. You will be able to communicate complex scientific findings clearly to different audiences and translate knowledge into practical approaches that can be embedded within Carelight. You will join a university community that values being inclusive, inspiring and impactful, where diversity strengthens the community and new ideas are encouraged.

The University of Lincoln is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join TwinHarvest, an innovative feasibility study investigating whether semi-transparent solar panels can be integrated into greenhouse structures to generate renewable electricity while maintaining crop performance.

Working at the interface of agriculture, horticulture and renewable energy, the project will evaluate the impact of spectrally selective organic photovoltaic (OPV) panels on strawberry crop growth and productivity, helping to assess the potential of this emerging technology for future sustainable food production systems.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute agricultural and crop science expertise to the design, delivery and analysis of glasshouse-based crop trials. Working closely with colleagues from engineering, energy and photovoltaic materials disciplines, you will evaluate plant and environmental responses under novel greenhouse conditions and help translate findings into evidence-based recommendations for future development.

You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in Agriculture, Crop Science, Horticulture, Plant Science or a related discipline, your experience of experimental research involving crop growth, plant physiology or agronomy will allow you to make a real contribution to this exciting project. You will be able to analyse and interpret scientific data, communicate findings effectively and work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research environment.

Job Purpose:

This role will support delivery of Bucks New University funded research project ‘AI & Medical Imaging’ by developing deep learning models for breast cancer classification using ultrasound imaging. The Research Assistant will assist with medical image data preparation, CNN model development and evaluation, cloud-based GPU training (including AWS), and research reporting and publication activities.  

 

 

Main Duties & Responsibilities of the role:  

Support the development and evaluation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for breast ultrasound image classification. 

Assist with the preparation, organisation, preprocessing and quality checking of ultrasound image datasets. 

 Implement and test deep learning experiments using Python and TensorFlow and/or PyTorch. 

Assist with GPU-based training and experiment management on AWS or other approved cloud computing platforms. 

Assess model performance using appropriate classification metrics and document experimental findings. 

Support reproducible research by maintaining clear code, experiment logs, model outputs and technical documentation. 

Contribute to reviewing scientific literature on medical imaging, CNNs and generalisation in breast ultrasound classification. 

Prepare research summaries, figures and presentations and contribute to manuscripts and other research outputs. 

Attend project meetings, communicate progress and collaborate effectively with the project team and partners. 

Handle research data securely and follow University policies, ethical approvals, data protection requirements and good research practice.

Comply with relevant legislative and other requirements (e.g., the Data Protection Act 2018 and GDPR; Health and Safety; UKVI; and Equality and Diversity) in all working practices.

Integrated van der Waals Nanochannels for molecular transport and sensing
About the role

We are recruiting a Research Associate to work on Integrated van der Waals Nanochannels for molecular transport and sensing. The successful candidate will join a newly established group at Imperial: you will build the platform together with the PI, shape the lab and its direction, and gain visibility.

Fluids confined to channels approaching molecular dimensions behave very differently from bulk liquids. Surface interactions, electrostatic screening and steric effects come to dominate, giving rise to anomalous transport and altered molecular behaviour. This project will exploit these effects by integrating van der Waals nanocapillaries with a microfluidic platform. The nanocapillaries are assembled layer by layer from two-dimensional crystals, giving atomically flat walls and channel heights controlled with sub-nanometre precision, while the microfluidic interface enables controlled delivery and exchange of analyte solutions. Using optical spectroscopy and electrical transport measurements, you will study how confined molecules respond to light and applied electric fields. By systematically varying channel dimensions, surface chemistry and solution conditions, the project aims to identify distinctive, measurable signatures suitable for highly sensitive and selective molecular detection

 

What you would be doing

You will be doing research on the integration of van der Waals nanochannels with microfluidic platform, then explore the molecular transport and sensing based on the integrated system, using a combined optical and electrical measurements.

You will study how confined molecules and structure and transport respond to pressure, light, or applied electric fields.

 

What we are looking for

Hold (or close to completion) a PhD in Condensed Matter Physics or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience *

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Experience:

Strong experimental expertise in the following areas:

Cleanroom nanofabrication;

Microfluidic system and ionic transport measurements;

Characterisation of 2D materials and their heterostructures;

A strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals and an ability to write scientific reports and contribute to writing research papers.

Skills and experience in instrument development

Desirable Knowledge, Skills, Experience and Qualifications:

Expertise in instrument automation.

Good understanding of theoretical condensed matter physics and statistical physics.

Expertise in molecular dynamics simulations.

The post is in Dr Qian Yang’s group in the Department of Physics, which works on transport phenomena and nanoconfinement effects inside nanocapillaries, in the field of nanofluidics.

Working under the direction of Professor Lisa Holmes, this work will examine relationships between the characteristics and needs of children aged under five and their families, patterns of multi-agency service access and engagement, and developmental and service outcomes. Role Description

We welcome applications for this exciting new post from passionate, prospective candidates to join our team working on Position, Navigation and Timing solutions to contribute to the projects in the area of multi-sensor resilient timing and navigation systems for aerospace applications.

About the Role

This post focuses on the development and validation of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) systems utilising a range of existing Cranfield facilities, such as Multi-User Environment for Autonomous Vehicle Innovation (MUEAVI), PNT simulator, Time and Frequency Innovation Node and supporting research project in the area of Intelligent Transport Systems, Autonomy, Navigation and Synchronisation for aerospace applications. As a Research Fellow, you will be developing prototype systems based on Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) components, designing and implementing into the prototype system algorithms for data acquisition, processing and fusion for a diverse range of sensors, including inertial, terrestrial and satellite navigation systems (e.g. IMU, GNSS, 5G, eLoran), software-defined (SDR) platforms and timing sources. You will also be supporting testing and validation activities utilising MUEAVI and London Cranfield Airport capabilities and mobile platforms for the delivery of research projects.

About You

You will be educated to PhD level (or close to completion) in Computer Science or Engineering areas related to signal processing for sensors or applications, and/or related disciplines, and have solid experience in estimation theory, signal processing and AI/ML with application to positioning and timing problems.

You will ideally have experience in sensor/signal/data processing for timing and positioning, and in design and development of simulation tools for timing and positioning applications.

With excellent communication skills, you will have expertise in implementing sensor data acquisition, processing, and hardware-based sensor fusion. A background in timing and positioning systems is important, with knowledge of machine learning applications in this area. Knowledge of timing and navigation system architectures and solutions utilising multiple sources of information, such as GNSS, LEO or 5G signals, would be a strong advantage. You will be confident in developing and using modelling and simulation tools for timing and positioning problems and be able to work both independently and as part of a team.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

Aerospace is at the heart of Cranfield’s global research airport and is renowned throughout the world for its teaching and research in the fields of aviation and aerospace. Cranfield Aerospace’s six Centres are the powerhouses of our world-class research, driving technological and conceptual advances in aeronautics, propulsion engineering, cyber-physical systems and intelligent automation. Through the strong links with industry built over the past 70 years, we focus on defining and delivering the aircraft, airport and airspace management of the future and are the only University in Europe with our own airport and runway. Cranfield Aerospace is internationally recognised as the first choice for research and education in all aspects of aerospace, including aircraft, drones, urban air mobility and space. Find out more about our work here.

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here.

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here.

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

How to apply                                           

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Professor Ivan Petrunin, Professor of Signal Processing and Intelligent Systems, on (E): i.petrunin@cranfield.ac.uk

Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on (E): peoplerecruitment@cranfield.ac.uk. Please quote reference number 5365.

Closing date for receipt of applications:   10 January 2027

Please note that we reserve the right to close this advert prior to the stated closing date should we receive sufficient numbers of applications. Therefore, we would encourage you to complete and submit your application as soon as possible.

 The successful candidate will join Dr Brandon Reeder's research group within the School of Life Sciences at the University of Essex from January 2027 as part of the UKRI-funded project A Tuneable Oxygen Carrier Platform for Emergency Care . The project aims to develop haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers with oxygen affinities tailored to clinical applications, including trauma care and sickle cell crisis.

 The School has established expertise in haemoglobin biochemistry, protein engineering, and translational biomedical research. Using facilities for recombinant protein production, fermentation, purification, and biochemical characterisation, the project will investigate the development of safe and effective oxygen therapeutics with clinical and commercial potential.   

 Duties of the Role 

 Research at the University of Essex will focus on the production, characterisation, and in vitro evaluation of engineered haemoglobin variants and haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers. Responsibilities include recombinant protein production in Escherichia coli , fermentation optimisation, protein purification, biochemical and biophysical characterisation, functional assessment of oxygen carrier performance, data analysis, publication writing, and delivery of project milestones. The postholder will also contribute to intellectual property generation, commercialisation and knowledge exchange activities, working closely with the University's innovation and enterprise teams to support translation of research outputs. The role will involve collaboration with academic collaborators and commercial partners involved in product development, translational strategy, and progression towards pre-clinical and clinical application. The postholder may also support student supervision where appropriate and will maintain high standards of laboratory practice, research integrity, health and safety, and regulatory compliance.

 Skills and qualifications required 

 We are seeking a highly motivated researcher with experience in protein biochemistry, biotechnology, microbial fermentation, recombinant protein production, or a related discipline. The successful candidate should have experience in the design, execution, and interpretation of independent research projects and be proficient in laboratory techniques relevant to recombinant protein production and characterisation. Experience of Escherichia coli expression systems, fermentation process development would be particularly advantageous. Experience in haemoglobin research, protein engineering, biotherapeutic development, translational biomedical research, or related areas would be beneficial but is not essential.

 The appointee will lead aspects of laboratory research, data analysis, and publication writing, while contributing to project management and activities supporting the translation and commercialisation of the technology.  Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Researcher to join the Dekker Research Group within the Department of Physics. The post is part of the ERC-funded DynaRep programme, which investigates the dynamics of DNA and chromatin replication at the single-molecule level. The work will provide a biophysically informed mechanistic foundation for understanding how the replisome can advance despite challenges along its DNA template.

 The successful applicant will conduct independent research into fundamental questions in genome biophysics, designing and carrying out experiments using single-molecule fluorescence microscopy and biochemical approaches, including protein purification and ensemble biochemistry. You will analyse experimental data using simulations and quantitative methods, test scientific hypotheses, and manage aspects of research projects to meet deadlines.

 You will contribute to the development of new research projects and ideas for generating research income, including presenting research proposals to senior researchers. You will also have opportunities to collaborate with researchers within the Department and across the UK, applying complementary techniques such as optical microscopy, cryo-EM and cross-linking mass spectrometry.

 You will contribute to high-quality publications, present research findings at scientific meetings, and work collaboratively within a small research team. You will also provide advice on scientific protocols and experimental techniques and support and mentor DPhil students.

 You will be able to manage your own academic research and associated activities, and have experience contributing to high-quality publications and presentations. You should be able to communicate research clearly, including writing for publication and presenting findings and proposals. You should be enthusiastic about contributing ideas for new research projects and potential research income.

 Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD/DPhil in biophysics or a closely related subject. Practical experience and scientific maturity in single-molecule fluorescence microscopy, protein purification and protein labelling are essential. Candidates should have research experience in at least one of the following areas: in-vitro biophysics, genome biology or single-molecule fluorescence. Strong conceptual and quantitative skills are required. Experience in biophysical assay development and optimisation, single-molecule FRET, chromatin biology, multi-protein in-vitro reconstitution, or single-molecule instrumentation development would be advantageous.

 The post is full-time and fixed term for 1 year initially, with the possibility of multi-year extension. The Dekker research group is based within the interdisciplinary Kavli Institute for Nanoscience Discovery at the University of Oxford.

 The University of Oxford is committed to equal opportunity, and to being an inclusive institution where everyone belongs and is supported to succeed. We recognise how the diversity of our community enriches our ability to deliver on our academic mission. We welcome applications from individuals from all backgrounds, including those who are under-represented within higher education. No applicant or members of staff shall be unlawfully discriminated against on the basis of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

 Applications for this vacancy are to be made online. You will be required to upload a covering letter/supporting statement addressing the selection criteria, your CV and the contact details of three referees as part of your application. For more information about the position, please contact Prof. Nynke Dekker, e-mail: nynke.dekker@physics.ox.ac.uk .

 The closing date for applications is 12 pm (UK time) on the for applications being noon on January 15, 2027 . Only applications received by this date will be considered. Interview arrangements will be communicated to shortlisted candidates.

Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the KPMG-Cambridge Partnership 'Future of Work': Mental Wellbeing Pillar (MWB). The position holder will be an integral member of the team led by Professor Gordon Harold with co-leads, Professors Qingyuan Zhao (Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics) and Diane Coyle (Department of Politics and International Studies). This particular position is associated with the data strand of the pillar and particularly methodologies for Causal Inference (working jointly with Professor Qingyuan Zhao).

The continuing focus on the use of data for policymaking means new methods are of vital importance to ensure that the best is made of the available data. It also provides an opportunity to bring together problems which traditionally are thought about in disciplinary silos.

The position is funded by the Cambridge-KPMG partnership to understand how the world of work is changing, starting with what really works when it comes to supporting employees' mental wellbeing, jointly between Cambridge and KPMG. Applicants are expected to have a PhD in a quantitative discipline (broadly interpreted including statistics, computer science, and quantitative social sciences) and demonstrable evidence of working across boundaries to solve real world problems. The role holder will be expected to plan and manage their own research and administration, with guidance if required, and to assist in the preparation of proposals and applications to external bodies. You must be able to communicate material of a technical nature and be able to build internal and external contacts. You may be asked to assist in the supervision of student projects, the development of student research skills, provide instruction or plan/deliver seminars relating to the research area.

Role Description

We welcome applications from skilled researchers to join our research on resilient and integrity-aware Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) solutions. The role will contribute to developing reliable timing and positioning capabilities for challenging operational environments, including those where GNSS is degraded or unavailable, with applications in critical national infrastructure, transport and autonomous systems.

About the Role

This post focuses on the development and validation of resilient multi-source PNT technologies, including research on reliable timing for airports and other critical infrastructure environments. The postholder will develop and evaluate signal processing, estimation and integrity monitoring algorithms for operation under interference and degraded or unavailable GNSS conditions. Research will consider complementary radio-navigation technologies such as eLoran, RF signal acquisition and processing, and sensor/information fusion.

The role will also involve the development of experimental PNT systems using software-defined radio (SDR) platforms, RF receivers, antennas and associated data acquisition equipment. You will plan and conduct simulations, laboratory experiments and field trials to assess performance, making use of Cranfield’s PNT facilities, including the Time and Frequency Innovation Node and the Digital Aviation Research and Technology Centre (DARTeC), and working closely with academic and industrial partners. You will also contribute to testing and validation activities utilising London Cranfield Airport capabilities.

About You

You will be educated to PhD level (or close to completion) in Engineering, Computer Science, Signal Processing, Telecommunications or a related discipline, with experience in signal processing, estimation or sensor data processing applied to positioning and timing problems. You will have demonstrated the ability to undertake independent research, and possess programming skills in MATLAB, Python, C/C++ or similar environments.

Ideally, you will have experience in navigation algorithm development, RF signal processing, multi-sensor integration or experimental PNT systems. Knowledge of resilient PNT, integrity monitoring, GNSS, eLoran, interference mitigation or AI/ML applications would be an advantage. Practical experience with software-defined radio (SDR) platforms, RF receivers, antennas, laboratory instrumentation or simulation tools would also be beneficial.

You will have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and evaluate algorithms, analyse experimental data and communicate research outcomes effectively. You will be able to work independently and collaboratively with academic and industrial partners, contributing to technical reports, research publications and successful project delivery.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

Aerospace is at the heart of Cranfield’s global research airport and is renowned throughout the world for its teaching and research in the fields of aviation and aerospace. Cranfield Aerospace’s six Centres are the powerhouses of our world-class research, driving technological and conceptual advances in aeronautics, propulsion engineering, cyber-physical systems and intelligent automation. Through the strong links with industry built over the past 70 years, we focus on defining and delivering the aircraft, airport and airspace management of the future, and are the only University in Europe with our own airport and runway. Cranfield Aerospace is internationally recognised as the first choice for research education in all aspects of aerospace, including aircraft, drones, urban air mobility and space. Find out more about our work here.

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here.

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here.

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

 About the Role 

 The Department of Education at the University of Oxford is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Researcher to join TEACHFORCE, a five-year European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant led by Professor Robert Klassen. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to an ambitious international research programme investigating teacher recruitment, motivation, and career exploration across England, Germany, and Hong Kong.

 TEACHFORCE explores how motivation shapes career exploration and decision-making, why individuals differ in their responsiveness to recruitment interventions, and how personalised approaches can support teacher recruitment. The project brings together advanced quantitative methods, longitudinal and experimental research, motivational profiling, predictive modelling, and AI-supported personalised interventions.

 The successful candidate will undertake advanced quantitative research, with particular responsibility for motivational profiling, predictive modelling, experimental and longitudinal analyses, and cross-national comparisons. They will also contribute to the development and evaluation of AI-supported personalised recruitment interventions, investigating individual differences in motivation, behaviour, and responsiveness to recruitment approaches.

 Working closely with Professor Klassen, the TEACHFORCE research team, and international collaborators, the postholder will coordinate defined research workstreams, contribute to theoretical and methodological development, and lead and collaborate on high-quality academic publications. The role also offers opportunities to develop independent research ideas, present findings at international conferences, and contribute to future research proposals.

 About You 

 You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD/DPhil in education, psychology, behavioural science, or a closely related discipline, with a strong quantitative research component. You will have specialist knowledge of educational psychology, motivational psychology, career development, or related areas of behavioural research.

 You will bring substantial experience in quantitative research design and advanced statistical analysis, including proficiency in R, Python, Mplus, or comparable statistical software. Experience in experimental research, longitudinal analysis, psychometrics, or latent-variable modelling is essential.

 You will also demonstrate knowledge of AI applications in psychological, educational, or behavioural research, including their potential use in research design, data analysis, predictive modelling, or personalised interventions.

 We particularly welcome applicants with advanced expertise in longitudinal or multilevel modelling, structural equation modelling, latent profile analysis, causal inference, or predictive modelling. Experience of motivational profiling, AI-supported research tools, gamified interventions, digital simulations, or interactive experiments would be advantageous, as would an understanding of responsible AI use.

 Knowledge of teacher recruitment, teacher education, career development, or occupational choice, and experience of comparative or cross-national research, would also be beneficial.

 You will have excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience contributing to academic publications and presentations, and the ability to manage independent research while collaborating effectively with interdisciplinary and international research teams.

 Application Process 

 Further information about the role, including the full job description and selection criteria, is available in the accompanying job description.

 Applications must be made through the University of Oxford's online recruitment portal. Applicants will be asked to upload a CV and supporting statement demonstrating how they meet the selection criteria, together with details of two referees.

 The closing date for applications is 12 noon (UK time) on Friday 18 December 2026.

 Informal enquiries about the post may be addressed to Professor Robert Klassen at robert.klassen@education.ox.ac.uk 

 The University of Oxford is committed to equal opportunity and to being a place where everyone belongs and is supported to succeed. We welcome applications from individuals from all backgrounds, including those under-represented within higher education.

 Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Assistant in Exoplanet Discovery with the PLATO Mission. The department of Physics invites applications for a PDRA to work with Prof. Suzanne Aigrain on the validation and scientific exploitation of data from the European Space Agency’s PLATO mission, focusing mainly on the impact of instrumental systematics and stellar variability on the detection and characterisation of transiting exoplanets.

 PLATO, due for launch in April 2027, will discover thousands of planets transiting bright stars, including habitable planets, and will probe the internal structure of the host stars using asteroseismology.

 The post-holder will work closely with Prof. Suzanne Aigrain, her research group, and collaborators at other PLATO Mission Consortium (PMC) institutes. They will take part in the scientific validation of PLATO’s data analysis pipelines, contribute to early science projects to demonstrate the mission’s performance, and help discover and characterise new exoplanets and their host stars with PLATO. The post-holder will be expected to participate in regular PLATO team meetings and telecons, to write scientific articles, technical notes, software and software definition documents, and to promote the mission and their research at international conferences. The post-holder will join a diverse, dynamic and supportive research group working on a range of topics related to exoplanet observations, in a world-class institution sporting a strong astrophysics and exoplanet community. The post-holder will have the opportunity to teach and supervise undergraduate research projects.

 Applicants should hold a PhD, or (be close to completion) in astrophysics or a related field and ideally a background in exoplanet or stellar observations. Applicants are expected to demonstrate excellent coding abilities, communication skills, and the ability to work well in a team. Previous experience in the field of transiting exoplanet discovery and characterisation will be an advantage, as will participation in large, collaborative software development projects.

 For direct enquiries about the role please contact Suzanne Aigrain, suzanne.aigrain@physics.ox.ac.uk

 We are currently inviting applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work with Professor Ben Green at the Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford.  The Role 

 Join the Leverhulme Trust-funded PeatFiRes project, examining how UK peatlands (Dartmoor, Peak District, Flow Country) respond to wildfire and recover over time. Leading the project’s Earth Observation and ecological modelling work, you will process multispectral imagery (Landsat, Sentinel-2), map plant functional types, apply statistical models (GAMs), and integrate satellite data with palaeoecological and climate records to identify resilience drivers, ecological thresholds, and climate impacts. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Acquire, process, and classify multispectral satellite imagery to map peatland disturbance and recovery.

 Perform time-series analysis on vegetation indices (NDVI, NDMI) to assess recovery trajectories.

 Build statistical and multivariate ecological models (GAMs) linking satellite, palaeoecological, and climate data.

 Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, open-access datasets, and stakeholder reports.   

 About You  

 PhD (completed or near completion) in Remote Sensing, Geography, Environmental Science, Ecology, or a related field.

 Technical proficiency in GIS, quantitative analysis, and programming (e.g., R, Google Earth Engine).

 Experience in remote sensing image processing, time-series analysis, or spatial modelling.

 Background in vegetation classification, wildfire ecology, change detection, or peatlands is desirable.   

 What We Offer 

 35 days annual leave + bank holidays & closure days.

 Generous pension scheme & flexible working options.

 Interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership opportunities, and dedicated researcher development support.

 How to Apply 

 Apply online with a supporting statement demonstrating how you meet the criteria.

 Closing date: 12 midnight, Sunday 10 January 2027

 About us 

 Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow (Band 7) position in the UCL Division of Infection and Immunity in the research team led by Prof. Paola Bonfanti currently based at the Francis Crick Institute .

 The Bonfanti lab is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join an exciting project investigating the role of thymus regeneration in healthy ageing and disease . Leveraging access to unique clinical cohorts and mouse models, we aim to dissect the critical role of the thymus in adaptive immunity reshaping how we understand tolerance and autoimmune disease onset. The post is funded by a European Research Council (ERC Advanced Grant, Horizon Europe Guarantee Scheme) research grant.

 Prof. Bonfanti directs an interdisciplinary team, across two main institutions. The proposed project stems from a joint collaborative effort with the University partner (UCL) and developed thanks to the Secondment programme UCL/Crick of the lead applicants who have access to all Science Technology Platforms (STPs) and Crick scientific environment.

 See https://www.crick.ac.uk/research/labs/paola-bonfanti for further background information.

 About the role 

 The post-holder will be expected to perform the highest quality research under the direction of the Principal Investigator, and to work effectively with internal and external collaborators involved in the project and other group members.

 The position is offered for 1 year in the first instance. The position may be extended, dependent on project success, and scientific priorities. The position will suit a motivated postdoctoral scientist who enjoys working as part of a multidisciplinary team and wishes to develop their career and pursue opportunities for independent fellowships.

 About you 

 The successful applicant should have a PhD or equivalent (or soon to be awarded) in Biology/Biomedical Sciences or a related subject and have significant experience working in a research laboratory.

 About us 

 The Fratta Lab, led by Professor Pietro Fratta, is a translational neuroscience research group based at the UCL Queen Square Institute of Neurology and the Francis Crick Institute, with strong clinical links to the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery. The Lab investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and related TDP-43 proteinopathies, with a particular focus on RNA biology, cryptic splicing and the development of novel therapeutic approaches.

 Our research spans fundamental discovery science through to clinical translation, with recent work contributing to the establishment of Trace Neuroscience, a biotechnology company advancing gene therapy approaches developed in the Lab towards clinical trials.

 About the role 

 We are seeking an ambitious and motivated Research Fellow to join an exciting two-year Target ALS-funded collaborative research project investigating the relationship between TDP-43 pathology and the immune system in ALS and inclusion body myositis (IBM).

 Building on the Lab's discovery that TDP-43-induced cryptic peptides can act as neoantigens and trigger cytotoxic T-cell responses, the project will investigate the mechanisms underlying this immune activation and its contribution to disease pathology. Working closely with collaborators at the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Miami and Mayo Clinic, the postholder will undertake molecular and immunological investigations, generate and analyse single-cell datasets from patient-derived samples, and contribute to the delivery and development of this research programme.

 This is an excellent opportunity to work at the interface of neuroscience, molecular biology and immunology within a highly collaborative international research environment.

 The role is available immediately and funded by the Target ALS for 12 months in the first instance.

 To apply, please upload a current CV, complete the online application form, and use the supporting statement section or upload a cover letter to outline how you meet the essential and desirable criteria for the role. Please do not upload any additional attachments as these will not be considered by the selection panel.

 About You 

 You will hold a PhD in Neuroscience, Molecular Biology, Immunology with relevant experience in molecular biology and immunological techniques. You will have practical experience in molecular cloning, screening and working with disease-relevant cellular or biological models. Experience in generating and analysing single-cell datasets is also needed.

 You will be an independent and motivated researcher with strong problem-solving, organisational and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary and collaborative research environment.

 This role meets the eligibility requirements for a skilled worker certificate of sponsorship or a global talent visa under UK Visas and Immigration legislation. Therefore, UCL welcomes applications from international applicants who require a visa.

 Appointment as Research Fellow is dependent upon having been awarded a PhD; if this is not the case, initial appointment will be as Research Assistant (salary £40,603 - £43,749 per annum) with appointment as Research Fellow being backdated to the date of final submission of the PhD thesis.
